explanation: Fires on a preposition that opens a new clause or sentence, usually 'In' (also 'At', 'During', 'in', Chinese 在) at the start of a sentence or answer (e.g. 'A:\n\nIn general', '. In addition', 'In order to', 'in turn'). Sentence-initial position after a period/newline gives the strongest activation; prepositions in the middle of a noun phrase ('vector in the transmission') are moderate to weak.

Hard to pin down. It fires on word-piece tokens in the middle of technical or foreign words (drug names, medical terms like th-al-assaemia, ritux-im-ab) and on function words in Norwegian/French/Spanish/German text (som ble, sont, har). It also fires on commas in drug lists. The common thread seems to be the middle of specialized or non-English text, but nothing predicts it well.

A mixture: code tokens (hash '$', generics commas, 'To' in camelCase, '.down', XML/XSL syntax, keys in brackets), the word 'subject' in PHP license headers 'This source file is subject to', and assorted English web boilerplate ('Thanks for visiting', 'send a link to', 'Buy New'). There is no single semantic theme.

Fires on the second or later piece of a proper name, i.e. a surname, place-name continuation or institution word that completes a known named entity (Elizabeth Warren, Ev-esham, Od-isha, Martin Luther King, Atomic Energy, Investor Protection, All Saints Church). Strongest on word-pieces inside rare names; weak on ordinary words.

No clear pattern. Top tokens include 'can', commas in lists, mid-word pieces of anatomical/medical terms (inferotemporal, soleus, atrioventricular, interleukin), Japanese nouns, '/' and 'and' in 'Intra- and inter-', and newlines in place lists. Many unrelated contexts.

Fires inside enumerations of counted items. It is strongest on the conjunction 'and'/'&'/',' joining the final members of a short list of names or numbers (Jono and Sushu, LmrC and LmrD, 66.7%, and 54), and on number words or digits that count a set ('three from the Grenadier', 'picking 2 w', 'first two-thirds'). Digits inside dates or measurements are weak.

Fires on the first sub-word piece of a word split into several tokens, especially an initial consonant cluster like 'St', 'sh', 'gr', 'b', 'p', 'D', 'F', or a first byte of a CJK/diacritic character. Activation is high when the word beginning is cut off from the rest (St-roop, sh-ivers, sh-udder, St. Joseph, Epstein-B-arr), and is unrelated to meaning.

Fires on verbs of wondering or uncertainty that introduce an indirect question, mainly 'wondering', 'wondered' and 'wonder' (as in 'I am wondering if/whether/how'). Close variants also fire: 'confused as to', 'puzzling over', 'unsure if', 'the question remains/is', 'trying to understand is'. Other question words without a verb of wondering are weak.

A mixture centred on structured or formatted strings: format specifiers in date/strftime code ('%Y', '('%', '[%'), digits inside postal ZIP codes in addresses, the commas and 'No.'/'OF' in legal case headers and dates, words in university/affiliation addresses ('Northeast Normal University', 'University of'), and identifiers in code (Aliyun, pygame). Ordinary prose is weak.

Fires on the stock words of software license and auto-generated headers: 'Licensed [under]', 'Apache [License]', 'under the [terms] of the GNU', 'See [the] License', 'This code was [generated]', 'go-sw[agger]'. A smaller second use is the stock words of award or honour titles ('Award for [Outstanding] Directing', 'Player [of] the Year') and 'bibli[ography]:' in paper metadata.

Fires on the head noun or key word-piece of a technical term, mostly inside a noun phrase that the context sets up (pharmac-okin-etic, 'tilt of the Earth', 'draft of the vessel', 'tops the ranking', 'Heap Based Buffer', 'integer division', 'bioavailability', 'Cauchy's integral'). It is broad and somewhat diffuse, with assorted prepositions after a technical verb ('diffracted by', 'backscattered from').

Mixed. It fires on package/import path tokens in Java/Kotlin/C++ ('org.jetbrains', 'java.awt.Color', '#include<iostream'), on the first katakana of Japanese loanwords and names, on brand or proper-name continuations (AFC Wimbledon, Fiat Chrysler, Colin Kaepernick), on 'External links', on '-less' suffixes and on 'granule'. Nothing ties these together.

Fires on the token just before a value or argument in templated or formulaic text: the space before a number ('picking 2', 'age of 21', 'Standard 2.0', '+0100', 'after 10 seconds'), 'an' in 'distributed on an "AS IS"' license boilerplate, and the token before an argument in code ('rotate(', 'fadeOut(', 'iter(['). Free prose is weak.

Mostly fires on mid-word pieces in Russian and Japanese text (сл-ож-ности, под-став-ьте, エ-ナジー, ダイ-ヤモ), plus a scattering of English and code tokens ('ever', 'every', 'twice', '!=', '.execute', digits after Tc-99/CO). The non-Cyrillic/CJK activations share no clear meaning.
